title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 180
paragraphs: Next to these Machlyes are the Auseans. These and the Machlyes live around Lake Tritonis, with the river Triton as the boundary between them. The Machlyes grow their hair long at the back of the head, the Auseans at the front. At an annual festival of Athena, their maidens take their stand in two parties and fight one another with stones and clubs, saying that in doing so they are performing the rites handed down by their fathers to the divinity who sprang from that land, whom we call Athena; and the maidens who die of their wounds they call “false-maidens.” But before letting them begin the fight, they do this: all together they equip the maiden judged fairest on each occasion with a Corinthian helmet and full Hellenic armor, and then, placing her in a chariot, they conduct her around the lake. I cannot say what they used to equip the maidens with in the old days, before the Hellenes settled near them, but I suppose they used to equip them with Egyptian armor—for it is from Egypt, I say, that both the shield and the helmet have come to the Hellenes. They say, moreover, that Athena is the daughter of Poseidon and of Lake Tritonis, and that she had some cause of complaint against her father and therefore gave herself to Zeus, and Zeus made her his own daughter. Such is the story these people tell; and they have their intercourse with women in common, not marrying but mating like cattle. When a woman's child has grown large, the men hold a meeting within three months of that time, and whichever of the men the child most resembles, his son he is accounted to be.
